bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices guide. No manufacturer manual exists for this model, so we built this from general best practices for this type of firearm. It does not represent manufacturer data. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take a firearm further apart than this guide goes unless its maker documents it.
cleanIntro:
No manual from Atlas Gunworks exists for this model, so this guide works from the pattern the Atlas Gunworks Erebus is built on — the 1911 — which comes apart the same way on every pistol of the kind, apart from one thing you can see at the muzzle. It clears the pistol, asks you to look, and strips it along the branch that matches what you see. If what you see matches neither, the slide stays on and the pistol is cleaned locked open.

Listed in Fieldstrip as 9mm. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Thumb safety down, magazine out, slide locked back
steps.action: On a 1911 the thumb safety locks the slide when it is up, so push it down before you work the slide — and remember it is never a substitute for an empty chamber. Press the magazine release and take the magazine out of the grip first. Then pull the slide fully back and push the slide stop up to lock it open. Magazine before slide, every time: the other way round puts a fresh round in the chamber.
steps.prose: If the magazine will not come out, stop and contact Atlas Gunworks, with the pistol pointed somewhere safe.

steps.title: Look, then feel — and do it twice
steps.action: With the action open, look into the chamber and down into the empty magazine well, then put a fingertip into the chamber: a cartridge that hides in a dark chamber cannot hide from a finger. Close the action under control, open it again, and check the same way a second time.
steps.prose: ⛔ If anything will not come out, stop: never pry it out with a tool, and contact Atlas Gunworks with the gun pointed somewhere safe.

steps.title: Bushing or no bushing? Look at the muzzle
steps.action: With the pistol empty, look at the front of the slide. One of two things is there: a separate round collar around the barrel — the bushing — with a short plug beneath it holding in the recoil spring; or no collar at all, the barrel's muzzle end thick enough to meet the slide on its own, usually with the end of a long guide rod showing beneath it. Follow the steps for what you see and skip the other.
steps.prose: ⛔ If you cannot tell, or you see something else, this is where your strip ends: leave the slide on and go straight to the cleaning steps, which work with the pistol locked open.

steps.title: Bushing: let the spring out under your thumb
steps.action: Only if yours has a bushing. Let the slide forward. Press the recoil spring plug in with your thumb and hold it there; with the other hand turn the bushing clockwise, seen from the muzzle, until it clears the plug — about a quarter turn. Then let the plug and the spring come forward slowly under your thumb, and lift them out.
steps.prose: ⛔ The plug is under real spring pressure and will fly if it slips: keep your thumb over it and the muzzle end away from your face. If the bushing will not turn by hand, a bushing wrench is the right tool — never pliers. If it still will not turn, or the plug will not come out past it, stop here: yours is set up differently.

steps.title: No bushing: capture the spring first, if yours needs it
steps.action: Only if yours has no bushing. Lock the slide open and look at the end of the guide rod showing under the barrel. If it has a small hole across it, slip the small pin the pistol came with — or a bent paperclip — through that hole, so the spring stays compressed on the rod. If the rod and spring are one sealed unit with no hole, there is nothing to do here.
steps.prose: ⛔ If there is a hole and you have nothing to put through it, stop: without it the spring comes out under full pressure.

steps.title: Slide stop out at the notch, slide off the front
steps.action: Draw the slide back slowly until the small half-moon notch on its left side lines up with the rear of the slide stop, and hold it there. Push the end of the slide stop's pin from the right side of the frame and draw the slide stop out to the left. Then run the slide forward off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: The notch is the only place the slide stop comes out: forced anywhere else it scratches a long arc into the frame — the mark every 1911 owner learns to avoid.

steps.title: Spring, guide rod and barrel out of the slide
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. With a bushing: lift the guide rod out from the rear, turn the bushing back the other way and lift it off, fold the barrel's link forward and draw the barrel out of the front. Without one: lift the captured spring and guide rod out with the pin still through it; the barrel comes out only if it slides out freely by hand — if it does not, leave it in, because the bore cleans perfectly well with it in place.
steps.prose: Note how each part sat before you move it; everything goes back the same way round.

steps.title: That is the whole strip
steps.action: Nothing else comes apart. The firing pin and its stop, the extractor, the hammer, the sear, the grip safety and the mainspring housing stay exactly as they are — on a pistol with no published procedure, those are work for Atlas Gunworks. Lay the parts out in the order they came off, on a clean cloth.
steps.prose: If any part came loose that this guide did not ask for, stop and contact Atlas Gunworks before you put the pistol back together.

steps.title: The bore, from the chamber end whenever you can
steps.action: With the barrel out, push a brush wet with bore solvent through from the chamber end, a few passes, then dry patches until they come out clean. If your barrel stayed in, clean it in the slide from the chamber end the same way, or with the pistol locked open feed a pull-through cord in at the chamber through the ejection port. Finish with a lightly oiled patch for storage, and run a dry patch through before you shoot.
steps.prose: The crown — the edge of the muzzle — is what decides where the shot goes; a rod dragged across it does lasting harm.

steps.title: Breech face, rails and the feed ramp
steps.action: Wipe the breech face — the flat at the back of the slide where the cartridge sits — and the slide's rails and the frame's rails with a cloth and a little solvent, using a small nylon brush on the carbon. Wipe the feed ramp and the barrel's throat until they are smooth and bright. Keep solvent out of the frame's internals and the firing-pin hole: what runs in there cannot be wiped back out.

steps.title: Oil lightly where metal slides on metal
steps.action: A thin film of gun oil goes on the slide rails, the frame rails, the outside of the barrel where it rubs the bushing or the slide, the barrel's locking lugs and its link. A drop is enough on each; wipe off anything that runs. No oil goes into the firing-pin hole or into the frame from the outside.
steps.prose: Too much oil collects grit and, in the cold, slows the parts it was meant to help.

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the slide, the frame and the barrel for cracks, the recoil spring for kinks or a broken coil, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for Atlas Gunworks.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until Atlas Gunworks has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Atlas Gunworks Erebus, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Atlas Gunworks exists for this model, so nothing about the inside of it can be known from a document. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to Atlas Gunworks, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush wet with bore solvent, from the chamber end
Dry patches until clean, then a lightly oiled patch for storage
A dry patch through before the next shot

cleaning.name: BREECH, RAILS & FEED RAMP
tasks: Breech face wiped, carbon off with a nylon brush
Slide rails and frame rails wiped
Feed ramp and barrel throat wiped smooth
⛔ No solvent or oil into the firing-pin hole or the frame's internals

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A thin film on the slide rails and the frame rails
A drop on the barrel where it rubs, on its locking lugs and on its link

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly: With a bushing: the barrel into the slide from the front, link folded forward; the bushing on and turned until it holds; the recoil spring and guide rod back in from the rear.
Without one: the barrel back if it came out; the captured spring and guide rod back under the barrel, the pin still through the rod.
The barrel's link tipped forward, the slide onto the frame rails from the front, and drawn back until the notch lines up with the slide stop's hole.

⛔ The slide stop pushed in from the left — it must pass through the hole in the barrel's link. If it will not go in with fingers, the link is not lined up: lift the rear of the barrel a little with a fingertip through the magazine well and try again; never hammer it.
With a bushing: the recoil spring plug pressed back in under your thumb and the bushing turned back to hold it. Without one: the slide locked open and the pin drawn out of the guide rod.
Work the slide several times with an empty magazine in: it should run smoothly and lock open on the empty magazine. Take the magazine out again.
fncheck: Magazine out and the chamber empty. Work the slide: it runs fully back and returns fully forward, and it locks open on an empty magazine. With the hammer back, the thumb safety moves up and down cleanly and holds in each position, and the grip safety springs back out when you let go of it. This check never asks you to press the trigger — whether to lower the hammer by dry firing is a question for Atlas Gunworks.
